fikir: Profesyonel bir tarih filmi sahnesi, 60 saniye. Fethin üçüncü günü, Haziran 1453, öğleden sonra. Topkapı'dan şehrin içine uzanan uzun, taş döşeli bir cadde; iki yanında balkonlu taş ve tuğla evler. Caddenin iki kenarında omuz omuza dizilmiş yeniçeri kordonu, ellerinde yalnızca tek beyaz hilalli, yıldızsız, yazısız kırmızı sancaklar; kordonun arkasında, balkonlarda ve pencerelerde binlerce Rum padişahı bekliyor: erkekler, kadınlar, yaşlılar, omuzlarda çocuklar; aralarında altı yaşındaki oğlunu kucağında tutan genç bir anne. Güneş caddenin sonundaki kapının arkasında; kapı puslu altın ışıkta parlıyor. Yüksek bir açıdan açılıyor: tören alayı kapıdan giriyor; önde ağır bir marş çalan mehter takımı, atlı çavuşlar, sancaktarlar ve yaldızlı alem; ortada beyaz atının üstünde genç Sultan II. Mehmed (21 yaşında, ince bıyıklı, kısa sakallı, gümüş zırh, kırmızı kaftan, beyaz sorguçlu miğfer), iki yanında yaya solaklar, sağ üzengisinde hocası Akşemseddin; arkada atlı vezirler ve paşalar, yeniçeri ağası. Alay caddeden kameraya doğru ilerledikçe kalabalık dalga dalga diz çöküyor. Alay caddenin ortasındaki küçük meydanda duruyor; mehter susuyor, ağır bir sessizlik. Akşemseddin: "Hünkârım, Peygamber efendimizin müjdesi bugün gerçek oldu." Sultan: "Bu zafer bizim değil, Allah'ındır." Sultan diz çökmüş binlerce kişiye bakıyor; anne oğlunu sıkıca tutuyor. Sultan yüksek, sakin ve güven veren bir sesle: "Kalkınız ve müsterih olunuz. Ben Sultan Mehmed; hepinize söylüyorum ki bu andan itibaren ne hürriyetleriniz ne de hayatlarınız hakkında korkmayınız." Binlerce kişi yavaşça ayağa kalkıyor; yine yüksek açıdan, bütün cadde. Kan, ceset, yaralı ya da yağma yok; ağırbaşlı, törensel ve gerçekçi.

mekan.tarif: A long, straight, gently rising street of worn stone paving inside Constantinople, seen from a high vantage point at its eastern end looking west down its whole length toward Topkapı. At the far end of the street the open brick-arched city gate in the land walls (pale limestone with red-brick bands) glows in hazy golden backlight. Both sides of the street are lined with two- and three-storey Byzantine stone-and-brick houses with timber balconies, wooden shutters and climbing vines. A continuous cordon of janissaries in crimson kaftans and tall white felt börk caps stands shoulder to shoulder along both edges of the street, facing inward, holding tall plain crimson banners that each bear only a single white crescent, no star and no writing. Behind the cordon, on the balconies and in the windows, thousands of townspeople stand packed and waiting: Greek men, women, old people and children on shoulders, in plain wool clothes of muted earth tones. The stone-paved centre of the street is empty. Halfway along, the street widens into a small square around an old marble fountain.

bloklar.ozet: High wide shot down the packed street: the ceremonial procession enters through the backlit gate, mehter playing. Then at street level among the waiting crowd: tense faces, the young mother with her son on her hip, the procession small and far away in the haze.

The procession advances up the street toward the camera in a symmetrical frontal composition, the Sultan centred on his white horse. As it passes, the crowd behind the cordon sinks to its knees in a wave. The procession halts in the small square; the mehter stops; heavy silence.
In the silent square, Akşemseddin looks up and speaks; the Sultan answers calmly. Close on the kneeling young mother pressing her son to her chest. The Sultan looks over the kneeling thousands.

The Sultan's ceremonial procession moves in strict order: at its head a mehter band on foot (kettle drums, big drums, zurnas, cymbals; red and green kaftans, tall caps) playing a slow, heavy march; then mounted heralds and standard-bearers with tall plain crimson banners bearing a single white crescent and a gilded alem finial; then the Sultan on his white horse, flanked on foot by two rows of solak guards in identical red kaftans and tall white plumed börk caps with bows across their backs, Akşemseddin walking at his right stirrup; behind him the viziers and pashas on horseback in long dark-green and deep-blue kaftans with large white turbans and grey beards, and the janissary ağa. Each group wears identical uniforms. Faces, armour, robes, the horse, the street and the crowd stay exactly the same as in the reference pictures. At the far end, in the hazy golden backlight of the open gate, the procession enters: first the mehter band, then the mounted standard-bearers with banners and a gilded alem, then <Subject 1> on his white horse between two rows of solak guards, <Subject 2> walking at his right stirrup, the mounted pashas behind. Small figures, moving slowly and in strict order.
[Shot 2] At 00:08.000, a locked-off street-level medium shot inside the crowd behind the cordon, 50mm lens, shallow depth of field. In the foreground <Subject 3> stands among tense, silent townspeople, her son on her hip; an old man beside her grips his cap; the red backs of the janissary cordon are just in front of them. Far down the street, out of focus in the golden haze, the procession approaches. At about 13.5 seconds everyone holds still until the end of the shot.
